name: Congenital Mitral Valve Insufficiency and/or Stenosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Mitral Valve Disease

criteria.description: Demonstration of abnormal mitral valve morphology including leaflet thickening, restricted motion, or clefts on echocardiography
Presence of mitral valve insufficiency (regurgitation) and/or stenosis confirmed by Doppler echocardiography
Clinical signs consistent with mitral valve dysfunction such as systolic murmur or signs of heart failure in infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal mitral valve morphology with evidence of insufficiency and/or stenosis on echocardiography
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Normal inflammatory markers unless secondary infection
imaging: Echocardiography showing mitral valve leaflet abnormalities, regurgitation jets, or stenotic valve orifice
Chest X-ray demonstrating cardiomegaly and pulmonary venous congestion
genetic: Possible association with mutations affecting cardiac valve development (e.g., NOTCH1 gene mutations)
other: Electrocardiogram may show left atrial enlargement or arrhythmias
Cardiac catheterization for hemodynamic assessment in complex cases

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset in childhood or adolescence

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
Development of atrial fibrillation or thromboembolic events
references: Moss and Adams' Heart Disease in Infants, Children, and Adolescents, 9th Edition
